surfaces.part: top header panel with blue and tan plaques
open display recess with hanging belts, ties and a bag

answer.evidence: The whole piece is drawn face-on. Rows 1-8 are a uniform tan header with a blue plaque and a tan plaque, both flat on the face with shaded lower rows. Rows 9-10 step from L=151 to L=128 as a front-facing cornice strip, with no lighter front-edge line and no eave shadow above a front face. Rows 11-24 are the flat recess with hanging items. Rows 25-29 are the drawer base. Only row 1 is a light outline-like rim, so there is no real top surface, and the piece matches the red 'front elevation: top 1' reference rather than the green cabinet.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows 14 visible tones per tile, between prop-hedge (9) and prop-stall-cheese (17) and a little below prop-well-roofed (20). Near-flat coverage is 8%, below the stall's 13%, so there are no large dead fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted brown beside the wood and tan frame rather than a black sticker line. By eye, the cream frame has a highlight, mid and shadow edge, and the hanging tools and padlock are drawn in separate tones. Its 24 total colours are fewer than the stall's 40 and the well's 38, and each material gets about 4 steps against the references' 5-6. That makes it slightly shallower, but a careful artist would still accept it beside the references, and it does not look thin or flat.

surfaces.part: header sign band with blue sign and tan plaque
darker ledge strip under the header
display recess with hanging ties and a bag

answer.evidence: The whole piece is drawn face-on at a constant width of 32 px for rows 1-30. The top band (rows 1-8) carries a blue sign and a plaque placed flat on its face, so it reads as a vertical header board. It has no back-to-front depth and no separate front-edge line. Rows 9-10 are only a 2-row darker ledge. The display recess (ties, bag) and the drawers below are all vertical faces. No ellipse, roof plane or visible contents of an open container shows a horizontal surface, so there is no real top surface and the drawing reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small wall-mounted cabinet with a tan/peach body, a darker brown frame, a few tool silhouettes and a padlock. Its measured facts are close to the references: 14 visible tones per tile against 17 for the stall and 20 for the well, near-flat coverage of 8% (stall 13%), and 0% neutral dark edges, so the outline is tinted brown rather than a black sticker line. By eye, though, the body panel is mostly 2-3 flat tones with little grain or speckle, and the frame has about 4 steps against the references' 5-6, so it looks flatter and simpler than the stall and well. It also lacks per-element shading on the hanging items. It is acceptable as a small simple prop, but I would not call it equal to the references. Because of the shallow panel shading and thin texture, I fail it when in doubt.

answer.evidence: The piece is drawn as a flat frontal elevation. Rows 1-8 are a header band, but the blue sign and tan plaque are drawn flat on it with their own shading, so it reads as a vertical signboard and not a horizontal top. Rows 9-10 are a cornice-like strip that works as a 1-2 row rim, not a top surface. Below it the display bay (rows 11-24) and the drawer base (rows 25-29) are all vertical faces. No ellipse, no receding side face, and no visible shelf or top plane.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small wall cabinet with a cream upper panel, a tan wood frame, a hanging tool rack and a padlock. It has 14 visible tones per tile, between the hedge (9) and the stall (17) and a little under the well (20). Near-flat coverage is 8%, below the stall's 13%, so there are no large flat fills. 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark brown that follows the wood, like the hedge and stall, rather than a black sticker line. Its ramps are somewhat shallower than the stall and well (about 4 steps against 5-6), and the texture is moderate, mainly wood grain and small tool details. A careful artist would still accept it next to the references without it looking noticeably thinner or flatter.
